1619.body:
I wonder what the proper way to handle this is because I'm pretty sure this is invalid syntax for having a path parameter in a route. If you look at the documentation (https://swagger.io/docs/specification/v3_0/paths-and-operations/) it says that curly braces are the only allowed way to include a path parameter so your spec should really have:
```
"/stuff/{action}": {
```
Or something similar. We could certainly make Counterfact handle this gracefully, maybe with a warning for invalid syntax, but I don't think we should allow Counterfact to accept this as a valid route. Do you have any agency in updating this spec? Maybe you can go to the maintainers of the spec and recommend they follow the correct syntax? If not that does make it challenging.
The swagger validator (https://editor.swagger.io/) doesn't fail the document, but it also doesn't show the parameter being recognized as a parameter.

@dethell
This is in fact no parameter - they just built an endpoint with URLs like this (and colons in URLs are perfectly valid).
Take following 2 endpoints as example:
```
POST /stuff/{stuffId}:duplicate
POST /stuff/{stuffId}:publish
```
Might not be perfect REST, but the API I'm working with has a lot of these cases.

Please also have a look at #1381, this fixed the problem of colons appearing in filenames (which is not allowed on Windows), but I feel this change somehow was not (successfully) applied to (at least) the import paths.

I guess you're right, the RFC for URIs does allow for the colon (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986). I learned something new today. We'll have to think on how to address this because we basically need to escape the `:` character with something allowed on the file system.

And if I see it correctly, there might be other problematic characters, e.g. it seems `*` is also allowed in URLs without percent-encoding, but forbidden in Windows filenames.

Not sure what a good solution is.
Map every problematic character to something else, like colon to ratio?
Or perhaps mask every "non-trivial" character somehow? (Well, find a nice defition of trivial... "small" set of characters we know are okay for filenames everywhere, like alphanumeric, braces, ...)
Perhaps just an encoding/masking for those characters that are known to be problematic for filesystems?

I think `<>:"\|?*` are the problematic characters for Windows, Linux/Mac don't really have problematic characters (perhaps just the null character) - and `/` is handled in a special way anyways.
Now we can discuss what is allowed in a URL and what some more or less sane developers might put in it anyways..

See here for even more interesting stuff about what might not be allowed on Windows:
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/naming-a-file#naming-conventions

Thanks for reporting this issue!

The colon in particular has come up before: https://github.com/pmcelhaney/counterfact/issues/1381

Let's start by making sure that works all the way through.

1617.body: Good catch. We'll need to gracefully fail if a reserved word is used. So either we fail fast up front and warn the user about the invalid spec or we handle it internally by somehow mogrifying the reserved word to something we can allow.

> [@dethell](https://github.com/dethell) I would prefer not failing because the OpenAPI spec is valid (at least [SwaggerEditor](https://editor.swagger.io/) gives no error). It is just not valid to use any `operationId` as identifier.
> 
> I guess it could be handled either by a special treatment for reserved words or by generally adjusting the mapping strategy from `operationId` to identifier (like perhaps adding a prefix).

I think you're right. It is valid in Swagger so we should work around it with a prefix or suffix.

> In our use case we're merging multiple YAML files before using Counterfact to generate types from them. Occasionally two different files will have two schema with the same name, in which case Counterfact silently generates only one `.ts` file, presumably corresponding to whichever schema it processed second (i.e. the second overwrites the first).
> 
> This failure mode can be tricky to detect manually, as often the two schema are similar enough in shape that it doesn't immediately cause TS errors. It would be nice if Counterfact would warn us by raising an error (detectable in CI) when it encounters multiple schema with the same name.

Jordan, do the two schema names have different paths within the spec? (I'd assume they'd have to for them to both survive the merging).

Oh, now I see that we're doing this differently than I thought. We're running `counterfact` multiple times on multiple YAML files with the same destination directory, and that's when the overwriting is happening.

Actually, it's kind of weird that you have a $ref that points to an object under paths. It would be better to put the definition of X-Request-Header and put it under components. 


```yaml

info:
  title: Cancellation API
  version: 2.0.0
paths:
  '/api/v2/{TestId}/cancel':
    put:
      operationId: cancelTest
      summary: Cancel a Test
      description: Method to cancel a test by its unique identifier.
      parameters:
        - name: TestId
          in: path
          description: A unique identifier for the test to be canceled.
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
        - name: X-Request-ID
          in: header
          description: >
            The `X-Request-ID` is used to track and identify individual requests
            as they traverse various systems to enable tracing.
          required: false
          schema:
            $ref: '#/components/headers/X-Request-ID/schema'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Successful cancellation of the test.
          headers:
            X-Request-ID:
              $ref: '#/components/headers/X-Request-ID'
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/CancelResponse'
        '400':
          description: Bad Request - Invalid input provided.
          headers:
            X-Request-ID:
              $ref: '#/components/headers/X-Request-ID'
          content:
            application/problem+json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required:
                  - type
                  - title
                properties:
                  type:
                    description: >
                      A string path which uniquely classifies the domain of the
                      error.
                    type: string
                  title:
                    description: A user-readable string title of the error type.
                    type: string
                  details:
                    description: >-
                      An array of strings providing additional details for the
                      error message.
                    type: array
                    items:
                      type: string
                  data:
                    description: >-
                      An array of objects providing additional data for the
                      error message.
                    type: array
                    items:
                      type: object
                      properties:
                        description:
                          type: string
                        element:
                          type: string
                        elementValue:
                          type: string
components:
  headers:
    X-Request-ID:
      description: >
        The `X-Request-ID` is used to track and identify individual requests as
        they traverse various systems to enable tracing.
      schema:
        type: string
        format: uuid
        example: 368b8d8f-5d07-4612-9523-d92fd57b0341
  schemas:
    CancelResponse:
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          type: string
          description: Message confirming cancellation.
          example: Cancelled successfully.
```
